frontMatter.purpose:
This New Life Medicals Private Limited Employee Handbook establishes policies, procedures, benefits, and working conditions that will be followed by all employees as a condition of their employment with New Life Medicals Private Limited. The Standards of Conduct describe the expected actions and behaviours of employees while conducting Company business.
This Employee Handbook is not a contract of employment nor is it intended to create contractual obligations for the Company of any kind. The handbook does not attempt to supersede or override any of the published or updated or concurrent policies or procedures of New Life Medicals Private Limited. It is meant to be a ready reckoner of all applicable employment related policies and procedures for the benefit of the employees. For all practical purposes, the policies available with HR or the respective owners of the Company policies will reign over anything published in this handbook.
The Company will make every effort to notify employees when an official change in policy or procedure has been made but employees need to proactively keep themselves updated by browsing through the Intranet where Company policies, procedures, benefits, and working conditions are updated.
The policies and procedures outlined in this handbook will be applied at the discretion of New Life Medicals Private Limited. New Life Medicals Private Limited reserves the right to deviate from the policies, procedures, benefits and working conditions described in this handbook. Furthermore, the Company reserves the right to withdraw or change the policies, procedures, benefits, and working conditions described in this handbook at any time, for any reason and without prior notice.

chapters.title: Confidentiality
chapters.text:
- All whistleblower complaints shall be handled with strict confidentiality.
- Information disclosed during investigations will only be shared with authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis.
- The identity of the whistleblower shall be protected to the maximum extent possible.
## Protection Against Retaliation
The Company strictly prohibits retaliation against any employee who reports concerns in good faith.
No employee shall face:
- Termination or demotion
- Harassment or intimidation
- Discrimination or unfair treatment
- Threats or victimization
Any act of retaliation against a whistleblower will result in disciplinary action.
## nvestigation Procedure
- All whistleblower complaints shall be formally acknowledged by the designated authority within 3 working days of receipt.
- A preliminary review and risk assessment shall be conducted within 7 working days to evaluate the nature, severity, and credibility of the reported concern.
- Based on the initial assessment, the Company may constitute an independent investigation committee comprising relevant internal authorities or external experts, wherever necessary, within 10 working days of receiving the complaint.
- All investigations shall be conducted in a fair, impartial, confidential, and independent manner. The investigation process shall ordinarily be completed within 30 working days; however, in complex cases requiring additional review, the timeline may be reasonably extended with proper justification.
- Employees, contractors, and relevant stakeholders are required to fully cooperate during the investigation process and provide accurate, complete, and truthful information whenever requested by the investigation committee or designated authority.
- Upon completion of the investigation, appropriate corrective, preventive, disciplinary, or legal actions shall be initiated based on the investigation findings within 15 working days of the final investigation report.
- The whistleblower, wherever appropriate and legally permissible, may be informed regarding the closure status or outcome of the investigation while maintaining confidentiality obligations.
## False or Malicious Complaints
The Company encourages responsible and genuine reporting. Knowingly making false, malicious, or misleading allegations may result in disciplinary action.
## Record Keeping
All whistleblower complaints, investigation records, findings, and actions taken shall be securely documented and maintained by the authorized department in accordance with applicable legal and company requirements.
## Employee Responsibility
Employees are expected to:
- Report concerns promptly and responsibly
- Act honestly and in good faith
- Maintain confidentiality during investigations
- Cooperate fully with authorized investigators
## Management Commitment
The Company is committed to fostering an ethical work culture where employees feel safe to raise concerns and contribute to a transparent, fair, and accountable workplace.
In order for Employees and all Executives to conduct company business and properly administer our own personnel procedures, Company must gather and maintain certain private information. The purpose of this Confidentiality Policy is to set forth guidelines with regard to the collection, maintenance, use and disclosure of confidential information. All employees share the responsibility to ensure that proper security and confidentiality are maintained. Report any breach promptly to the Human Resource Department or to the concerned authority. Anyone who violates this policy will be subject to disciplinary action and possible legal recourse.
Company property includes not only tangible property such as desks and computer terminals, but also intangible property such as information and data on those computer terminals. Of particular importance are proprietary information and confidential information. Proprietary information includes all information obtained by company employees during the course of their work. Customer lists and files, production information, personnel files, employee medical information, computer records, financial and marketing data, formulae and trade secrets are examples of confidential information.
## General Policies
- Employees and all Executives must not disclose or use proprietary or confidential information except as the job requires. They also may not disclose or use any proprietary or confidential information that they obtain during the course of their employment with any previous employer.

chapters.title: Employment Categories
chapters.text:
Each employee will belong to one other employment category given below:
## Regular full-time employees
Regular full-time employees are those who are not in a temporary or probation status and who are regularly scheduled to work company full-time schedule. Generally, they are eligible for company benefit package, subject to the terms, conditions, and limitations of each benefit program.
## Probation employees
Probation is those whose performance is being evaluated to determine whether further employment in a specific position or with company is appropriate. Employees who satisfactorily complete the probation period will be notified of their new employment
## Contractual Employees
Contractual employees are those who are hired as interim replacements, to temporarily supplement the work force, or to assist in the completion of a specific project. Employment assignments in this category are of a limited duration. Employment beyond any initially stated period does not in any way imply a change in employment status. Temporary employees retain that status unless and until notified of a change. While temporary employees receive all legally mandated benefits, they are ineligible for all of company other benefit programs.
## Management Trainees
Management Trainees are those who are recruited for a period of 1 to 3 months from Management colleges.
## Promotions
New Life Medicals Private Limited strives to promote the most capable and experienced employees based on their demonstrated ability to assume greater responsibility and perform essential job tasks. Consequently, reasonable efforts will be made to fill vacant positions from within the Company wherever possible. At the same time, the Company may recruit externally in order to attract the most qualified individual for a particular job vacancy.
All job openings shall be posted on Company bulletin boards and other communication platforms accessible to employees. Simultaneously, external recruitment sources may also be utilized.
To be eligible to apply for a posted vacancy, employees must meet the minimum qualifications and hiring specifications for the position, have successfully completed their introductory period, and maintain good standing in terms of overall work performance, conduct, and compliance with Company policies.
Selections for promotions, transfers, and career advancement opportunities shall be made based on an individual’s qualifications, skills, experience, performance, competency, and ability to perform the essential duties of the role.
The Company is committed to ensuring that all promotion and transfer decisions are conducted in a fair, transparent, and non-discriminatory manner. No employee or applicant shall be discriminated against or denied equal opportunity in the promotion process on the basis of race, caste, religion, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy, age, disability, nationality, ethnic origin, political opinion, or any other characteristic protected under applicable laws. The Company shall promote equal opportunity and merit-based career progression across all levels of employment.

chapters.title: Open Door Policy
chapters.text:
New Life Medicals Private Limited has adopted an Open Door Policy for all employees. This means, literally, that every manager's door is open to every employee. The purpose of our Open Door Policy is to encourage open communication, feedback, and discussion about any matter of importance to an employee. Our Open Door Policy means that employees are free to talk with any manager at any time.
If any area of your work is causing you concern, you have the responsibility to address your concern with a manager. Whether you have a problem, a complaint, a suggestion, or an observation, your company managers want to hear from you. By listening to you, the company is able to improve, to address complaints, and to foster employee understanding of the rationale for practices, processes, and decisions.
Most problems can and should be solved in discussion with your immediate supervisor; this is encouraged as your first effort to solve a problem. But, an open door policy means that you may also discuss your issues and concerns with the next level of management and/or Human Resources staff members. No matter how you approach your problem, complaint, or suggestion, you will find managers at all levels of the organization willing to listen and to help bring about a solution or a clarification.
## Rehiring Policy
A former employee who has been rehired after leaving employment for more than one calendar year is considered an introductory employee during their first ninety days following rehire. The benefits may or may not be continued from the point of their last tenure unless required by law. In effect, the Company is not required to owe any returning employee for previous time earned for vacation, sick, etc.
Any employee returning to work after a leave of less than one calendar year will have their benefits reinstated at the level when separation began; less any time owed back to the company. This is intended to help employees who have been laid off due to unforeseen Company circumstances. Other circumstances may affect the Company's decision to reinstate benefits except for those governed by law.
## Management Trainee Policy
New Life Medicals Private Limited Follows a Management Trainee Policy wherein students from leading management schools / Pharma College are recruited for a period of 1-6 months every year. Such recruitments would be project- based. New Life Medicals Private Limited does not provide stipend to such recruits but the trainees may be absorbed if found competent.
## Personnel file policy
A personnel file is maintained for each employee of New Life Medicals Private Limited. These personnel files contain confidential documents and are managed and maintained by Human Resources staff.
Typical documents in a personnel file include the employment application, a family emergency contact form, documented disciplinary action history, a resume, employee handbook and at-will employer sign off sheets, current personal information, and job references. Not all personnel files contain the same documents but each personnel file has some documents that are the same.
Payroll files are also maintained; payroll files contain a history of the employee's jobs, departments, compensation changes, and so on.
An employee may view his or her personnel file by contacting a Human Resources staff person during normal business hours. No employee may alter or remove any document in his or her personnel file which must be viewed in the presence of an HR staff person.
## Access to Personnel Records
All employees, former employees, and representatives of employees may view certain contents of their personal file with advance notice to Human Resources staff. Documents that relate to the employee's qualifications for hire such as the application, promotion, disciplinary action, and transfer may be viewed. Additionally, the employee may review policy signoff forms and training records.
Documents that the employee may not review include: references or reference checks, records of any investigation undertaken by management, medical records, documents related to a judicial proceeding, any document that would violate the confidentiality of another employee, and documents used for employee planning.
## Employee Document Retention Schedule
[table]
| Document Type | Retention Period | Applicable Reference / Law |
| Personnel Files | Employment Period + 3 Years | Company Requirement |
| Attendance & Leave Records | 3 Years | Factories Act / Shops & Establishment Act |
| Payroll & Salary Records | 8 Years | Income Tax Act, 1961 |
| PF & ESI Records | 5 – 7 Years | EPF Act, 1952 & ESI Act, 1948 |
| Training Records | 3 Years | ISO / Internal Compliance Requirement |
| Disciplinary & Grievance Records | 5 Years | Internal HR Compliance Requirement |
| Health & Safety Records | 5 Years | Factories Act, 1948 / OSHA Requirements |
| Resignation & Separation Records | 5 Years | Labour Law & Audit Requirement |

chapters.title: Working Hours
chapters.text:
The office working hours are as follows:
[table]
| Shift | Time |
| Regular Shift | 10:00 AM to 07.00 PM |
Certain employees may be assigned to different work schedules and/or shifts outside of normal office hours. If an employee must be outside of the office for non-business-related reasons during their normal work schedule, they should inform their manager.
To maintain decorum in the office the organization requests every employee to be on time. Regular Late arrival by more than 15 minutes will be seriously viewed and disciplinary action may be taken.
If there are more than 4 Late Marks in a week it would be considered as a half day.
## Break and Lunch Hours
Lunch time at the office is between 1 PM to 2 PM. All employees are required to strictly follow the lunch time and not engage in taking frequent breaks during working hours as it affects the overall working of the company.
## Attendance Expectations and Policies
Excellent attendance is an expectation of all employees of New Life Medicals Private Limited Ltd. Emergency personal time is made available to employees for such unscheduled events as personal illness, immediate family member illness, and doctor appointments.
## Telecommuting Policy
The Company is committed to creating a work environment where the needs of our customers, employees, and the Company are balanced. Therefore, the Company tries to be flexible in its approach to work styles and location. Telecommuting arrangements may be made on an “as needed basis” or set up on a regular schedule. In either case, employees are encouraged to spend time working in the office whenever possible. This allows employees to be accessible to customers and creates a sense of consistency and collaboration among work teams. When employees desire to work at home, the Company asks that they do so in a manner which is in keeping with a work style of accessibility, communication, and productivity. All Telecommuting arrangements are subject to approval by the employee’s manager. In general, the following principles should be used in Telecommuting:
- Employees should make arrangements with their manager at least one week in advance of Telecommuting.
- Employees should check in with the office regularly.
- Employees should inform their manager of their whereabouts so they may be reached easily.
- Working at home means working, not taking time off.
- Under regular circumstances, Telecommuting should not comprise more than one day in a given week, or more than 3 days a month.
## Working Hours, Attendance Monitoring and Overtime Management
The Company is committed to maintaining proper working hour management practices in compliance with applicable labour laws and operational requirements. Employee attendance, working hours, and overtime activities are regularly monitored to ensure operational efficiency, employee wellbeing, and legal compliance.
The Company currently manages working hours and attendance through:
- Maintaining regular attendance records for all employees through attendance registers and internal monitoring systems
- Daily monitoring of employee in-time, out-time, shift timings, and attendance status by HR and reporting managers
- Reviewing regular late arrivals, absenteeism, and attendance irregularities through periodic attendance checks
- Monitoring employee working hours to ensure compliance with approved office timings and shift schedules
- Communicating attendance expectations and workplace discipline requirements during onboarding and internal discussions
- Reviewing employee leave records, attendance summaries, and working hour reports on a regular basis
- Monitoring overtime work requirements and obtaining management approval wherever overtime is operationally necessary
- Ensuring overtime work, wherever applicable, is controlled, recorded, and managed in accordance with operational requirements and applicable regulations
- Encouraging employees to maintain punctuality and proper attendance discipline across all operational locations
- Conducting coordination between HR, management, and departmental heads regarding attendance management and workforce planning
## Overtime Policy and Compensation
The Company may require employees to work beyond regular working hours in situations such as urgent operational requirements, month-end closing activities, audit preparation, inventory verification, dispatch planning, customer commitments, compliance deadlines, or other business-critical requirements.
Overtime work shall only be performed with prior approval from the concerned reporting manager or management authority. Unauthorized overtime work shall not be considered for overtime payment or compensation.
The Company currently manages overtime practices through:
- Daily monitoring of employee attendance, in-time, out-time, and working hours through attendance registers, biometric systems, and internal attendance tracking records

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangement
chapters.text:
The Company is committed to promoting a flexible, inclusive, and employee-friendly work culture to support employee wellbeing, operational efficiency, and work-life balance, wherever reasonably practicable and operationally feasible.
Subject to business requirements and management approval, the Company may offer the following flexible work arrangements:
- Flexible working hours / staggered office timings
- Hybrid working model (combination of office and remote work)
- Work-from-home arrangements for eligible roles
- Shift flexibility based on operational requirements
- Temporary flexible schedules for medical, maternity, paternity, caregiving, or personal requirements
- Role-based remote working arrangements for approved departments or projects
## Eligibility Criteria
Flexible work arrangements may be considered for employees meeting the following criteria:
- Employees who have successfully completed their probation period, unless otherwise approved by management
- Employees whose job responsibilities can be effectively performed under flexible or remote arrangements
- Employees maintaining satisfactory performance, productivity, attendance, and disciplinary records
- Employees capable of ensuring confidentiality, data protection, and adherence to Company policies while working remotely or flexibly
- Employees having reliable internet connectivity, communication accessibility, and a suitable working environment, wherever remote working is permitted
## Approval & Resource Availability
- Flexible work arrangements shall be subject to departmental requirements, operational feasibility, client commitments, workflow dependency, and availability of technological resources
- Approval shall be granted based on reporting manager recommendation and management / HR approval
- The Company may provide necessary tools, software access, communication systems, or IT support based on role requirements and resource availability
- Certain departments, manufacturing functions, operational roles, customer-facing positions, or site-based activities may not be eligible for all categories of flexible work arrangements due to business and operational requirements
- The Company reserves the right to review, modify, suspend, or withdraw flexible work arrangements at any time based on operational needs, performance concerns, misuse, policy changes, or business continuity requirements
## Compliance & Cancellation of Flexible Work Arrangement
- Employees availing flexible work arrangements shall remain accountable for productivity, availability during working hours, timely communication, attendance in meetings, and completion of assigned responsibilities
- All Company policies relating to confidentiality, information security, code of conduct, health & safety, and professional behaviour shall continue to apply during flexible work arrangements
- Any misuse, policy violation, misconduct, data confidentiality breach, repeated productivity concerns, unauthorized absence, communication failure, or non-compliance with Company requirements during flexible working arrangements may result in immediate cancellation or withdrawal of the flexible work benefit
- The Company reserves the right to discontinue or revoke flexible work arrangements for any employee or department in case of operational disruption, disciplinary concerns, or violation of Company policies and procedures
## Conditions
- Flexible work arrangements are a business privilege and shall not be treated as a permanent entitlement or guaranteed employee benefit
- Employees must remain available and reachable during agreed working hours and attend meetings, reviews, and official communications as required
- Employees working remotely shall comply with all IT security, cybersecurity, confidentiality, and data protection requirements of the Company
- The Company may periodically review the effectiveness, productivity, and business impact of flexible work arrangements
- Flexible work arrangements may be approved for a temporary, project-specific, or review-based period depending upon business requirements
- Employees are expected to maintain a safe, professional, and distraction-free working environment while working remotely
## Workplace Professionalism and Company Representation
## Work Dress Code
The Company's objective, in establishing a dress code, is to enable employees to project a professional, business-like image while experiencing the advantage of more casual and relaxed clothing. Business casual dress is the standard for this dress code
Semi- Formal: In general, consider the following:
- Clothing should be conservative and nice. Button-down shirts, trousers, blouses, sport coats, and skirts are suitable.
- Keep skirts knee-length or longer.
- Tie is not necessary
The company policy allows casual dressing on every Friday and Saturday
Casual: Casual still means work-appropriate, so your clothes must still be neat and conservative.

chapters.title: Use of Company Equipment and Electronics
chapters.text:
## Telephone Use
Company employees may receive or make personal telephone calls during break periods only. If a telephone call is received during a non-break time, and the call is not an emergency, callers will be asked to leave a message.
Please inform your family and friends of this company policy and request that they keep these telephone calls to a minimum during work hours.
In the instance of a legitimate emergency telephone call during work hours, we will immediately attempt to locate that employee to receive the call.
Phones provided at work stations are to be used to conduct company business.
The employee telephones in the break rooms are available to make outgoing, local, personal calls during break times.
## Cell Phone Policy
This policy about cellular phone usage applies to any device that makes or receives phone calls, leaves messages, sends text messages, surfs the Internet, or downloads and allows for the reading of and responding to email whether the device is company-supplied or personally owned.
An employee who uses a company-supplied device or a company-supplied vehicle is prohibited from using a cell phone, hands on or hands off, or similar device while driving, whether the business conducted is personal or company-related. Use of company owned vehicles or devices for personal business is discouraged.
Your company is aware that employees utilize their personal or company-supplied cellular phones for business purposes. At the same time, cell phones are a distraction in the workplace. To ensure the effectiveness of meetings, employees are asked to leave cell phones at their desk. Or, on the unusual occasion of an emergency or anticipated emergency that requires immediate attention, the cell phone may be carried to the meeting on vibrate mode.
## Company Tools, Equipment and Supplies
Electronic equipment, including but not limited to computers, telephones, pagers, printers and fax machines, used or owned by the company and all information stored on this equipment is company property. Company reserves the right to review and disclose any information sent, received or stored on this equipment.
Much of the information stored in the company’s electronic equipment is confidential; disclosure can only be made at the company’s discretion, any unauthorized disclosure to outsiders or co-workers is prohibited.
Copying software programs and downloading programs or information from the Internet can result in copyright violations or viruses. You are strictly prohibited from making any copies of software without prior approval of the Systems Administrator. Installing software from home on company equipment is also forbidden. Any software programs that you wish to install on company electronic equipment must first be registered with the Systems Administrator.
Deleting information from electronic equipment usually does not mean that it has been permanently destroyed. Information that you would be embarrassed revealing to co-workers, a jury or family members should never be sent, stored or received on the company’s electronic equipment.
## Computer and Internet Use Policy
Voice mail, email, and Internet usage assigned to an employee's computer or telephone extensions are solely for the purpose of conducting Company business. Some job responsibilities at the Company require access to the Internet and the use of software in addition to the Microsoft Office suite of products. Only people appropriately authorized, for Company purposes, may use the Internet or access additional software.
## nternet Usage
Internet use, on Company time, is authorized to conduct Company business only. Internet use brings the possibility of breaches to the security of confidential Company information. Internet use also creates the possibility of contamination to our system via viruses or spyware. Spyware allows unauthorized people, outside the Company, potential access to Company passwords and other confidential information.
Removing such programs from the Company network requires IT staff to invest time and attention that is better devoted to progress. For this reason, and to assure the use of work time appropriately for work, we ask staff members to limit Internet use.
Additionally, under no circumstances may Company computers or other electronic equipment be used to obtain, view, or reach any pornographic, or otherwise immoral, unethical, or non- business-related Internet sites. Doing so can lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.
## Email Usage at Company
Email is also to be used for Company business only. Company confidential information must not be shared outside of the Company, without authorization, at any time. You are also not to conduct personal business using the Company computer or email.
Please keep this in mind, also, as you consider forwarding non-business emails to associates, family or friends. Non-business related emails waste company time and attention.

chapters.title: Learning, Training & Development
chapters.text:
The Company believes that continuous learning and skill enhancement are essential for employee growth, operational excellence, and organizational success. Accordingly, the Company provides training and development opportunities based on business requirements, technological advancements, operational needs, and employee competency development.
- Employees are provided technical, functional, behavioral, safety, compliance, leadership, quality, ESG, and role-specific training programs as identified by the Company
- Training needs are identified through performance evaluations, departmental assessments, business requirements, audits, compliance obligations, and management recommendations
- Employees are required to attend mandatory training programs assigned by the Company
- The Company conducts internal training sessions, external workshops, online learning programs, certifications, seminars, and on-the-job skill development initiatives
- Participation in training programs forms part of employee development and performance improvement initiatives
- The Company nominates employees for specialized training programs based on role criticality, succession planning, and organizational requirements
- Employees are expected to actively participate in learning initiatives and apply acquired knowledge and skills in their professional responsibilities
New Life Medicals Private Limited recognizes the importance of training their employees for effective and more efficient working. The Company also engages in regular training and development programs for their employees. The training requirement can be either cited by the authorized managers according to the need to a group of employees or;
Self-initiated by the employee who wishes to be trained in a particular area.
## Business / Sales Call
The employees who are required to go for business calls need to maintain a Customer Visit Report (CVR) with the Human Resource Department. Each Business Call made has to be verified by the Customer Visit Report at the time of claiming the expenses.
## Deputation Policy
If the Company feels the need, employees can be deputed to another department or region for a maximum of 3 months. In case of deputation to another region, the respective regional head is responsible for arranging the accommodation and other facilities. All deputations need to be pre-approved by the Business Head and the CEO.
All deputations need to be planned 15 days prior to deputing for the smooth operation of the process.
## Employment Termination
Employment Termination at New Life Medicals Private Limited would fall under one of the following categories:
Dismissal: On account of any misconduct as specified in the employee handbook or if the employee is absconding for more than 15 days, the employment would be terminated immediately without further notice.
Resignation: If the employee wishes to separate from the Company, He/she is required to put in his/her resignation and continue service during the notice period as specified in the Offer/ Appointment letter
Discharge: Constant ill-health or permanent disability of the employee can result in Discharge of the employee from the organization. The employee separating from such circumstances is entitled to receive one month’s basic salary post his separation.
Voluntary Retirement Scheme: New Life Medicals Private Limited offers a voluntary retirement scheme to its employees in compliance with the statutory standards.
## Exit Interviews
The employment termination is carried out according to the Exit Booklet which requires the employee to submit the customer contact lists, return the company assets and sign offs from all the departments.
The employee is required to go through an Exit interview conducted by the Human Resource Personnel.
## Supplier Code of Conduct
The Company expects all suppliers, vendors, and business partners to adhere to ethical and responsible business practices.
- Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations
- Prohibition of child labour, forced labour, and unethical practices
- Maintenance of integrity, transparency, and fairness in business dealings
- Respect for environmental and social responsibilities
Failure to comply may result in termination of business relationships.
## Payroll Information
## Compensation Schedule
- Salary: The salary of every employee will be given 7th of Subsequent Month
- LTA: Employees can claim LTA once in four years i.e. between 1st April to 31st March.
- Performance Incentive: Employees are entitled to receive Performance Incentives based on their performance throughout the year. A separate Incentive Structure will be shared with all the employees The incentive is disbursed once in a year.
- All employees who fall under the Income Tax should submit their Investment Plans by May of every financial year.
- All the Investment Plan proofs need to be submitted by the end of January.

chapters.title: Performance Management System
chapters.text:
Performance of the employees will be judged on KRAs and other behavioral competencies. At New Life Medicals Private Limited, we have a Performance Appraisal conducted every 6 months. The Procedure would be as follows:
- Every Employee is given a set of KRAs in consultation with the respective Department Heads.
- At the end of 6 months, each employee is evaluated on the basis of his/her performance with respect to the predetermined KRAs.
- Performance Incentives and Performance awards are disbursed on the basis of the Performance Appraisal of the employees.
## Career Development Plan
The Company supports employee career growth and professional development through structured performance reviews and development planning.
- Following the annual performance evaluation process, a Career Development Plan (CDP) is prepared for employees based on performance outcomes, competency assessment, potential evaluation, and business requirements
- The Career Development Plan includes role enhancement opportunities, skill development requirements, leadership development initiatives, succession planning, mentoring, cross-functional exposure, and training recommendations
- Individual development objectives and growth plans are discussed between the employee, reporting manager, and HR department
- Career progression opportunities are determined based on employee performance, behavioral competencies, business requirements, organizational structure, and management discretion
- Preparation of a Career Development Plan does not guarantee promotion, salary increment, role change, or transfer
## Employee Conduct and Performance
- Report to work as scheduled and seek approval from their supervisors in advance for any changes to the established work schedule, including the use of leave and late or early arrivals and departures.
- Perform assigned duties and responsibilities with the highest degree of public trust.
- Devote full effort to job responsibilities during work hours.
- Maintain the qualifications, certification, licensure, and/or training requirements identified for their positions.
- Demonstrate respect for the agency and toward agency co-workers, supervisors, managers, subordinates, residential clients, students, and customers.
- Use company equipment, time, and resources judiciously and as authorized.
- Support efforts that ensure a safe and healthy work environment.
- Utilize leave and related employee benefits in the manner for which they were intended.
- Resolve work-related issues and disputes in a professional manner and through established business processes.
- Meet or exceed established job performance expectations.
- Make work-related decisions and/or take actions that are in the best interest of the Company
## Conflict Resolution
Each person employed by the Company shall not engage in any activity if it will:
- Adversely affect on-the-job work performance,
- Create a conflict with the business interests and purposes of the company or
- Have a negative impact on the business or reputation of the company, its product or other company employees.
## Complaint Procedure
- The HR Personnel is designated as the person who will receive a complaint from any employee who believes that his or her personal information or privacy has been compromised or that any employee has violated this privacy policy. The concerned Authority has the responsibility of conducting a proper investigation.
- An employee may make a complaint by directly approaching the aforementioned authority
- When a violation has occurred, the Company will mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect of the disclosure and will apply appropriate sanctions.
## Employee Mobility
The Company promotes internal career growth and provides employees with opportunities for various types of internal mobility based on organizational requirements, employee capability, and performance evaluation outcomes.
- Vertical Mobility – Movement of an employee to a higher role, designation, responsibility level, or leadership position through promotion based on performance, competency, experience, and organizational requirements
- Horizontal Mobility – Transfer of an employee to a similar level role across departments, functions, or teams for cross-functional exposure, skill enhancement, and business requirements
- Cross-Functional Mobility – Movement of employees between different business functions or departments to enhance organizational exposure, capability development, and operational collaboration
- Geographical / Location Mobility – Transfer of employees between office locations, project sites, manufacturing units, warehouses, or operational facilities based on business and operational requirements
- Project-Based Mobility – Temporary assignment of employees to specific projects, task forces, audits, implementation teams, or strategic initiatives for defined business objectives

chapters.title: Provident Fund
chapters.text:
All employees are covered in compliance with the Provident Fund Act of 1952 according to which:
Employee’s Contribution: 12% of the Basic Salary. The employee can opt for additional contribution towards Provident Fund via Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF)
Employers’ Contribution: 12% of the Basic Salary of the Employee
Gratuity will be paid in compliance with the Payment of Gratuity Act of 1972 to all eligible employees of New Life Medicals Private Limited The employer shall pay gratuity to the eligible employee for every completed year of continuous service (more than 5 years) at the rate of 15 days salary per completed year of service. The rate of salary shall be the rate of last drawn salary.
## ESIC
All eligible employees are covered in compliance with the ESI Act of 1948. All employees drawing a monthly salary up to Rs. 15,000 per month are coverable under the ESI scheme.
Employee’s contribution: At the rate of 1.75% of Salary Employer’s Contribution: At the rate of 4.75% of Salary.

## Employee Well-being and Family Support

The Company also promotes awareness on:

- Healthy workplace practices

Employees are encouraged to seek support whenever required.
The Company recognizes the importance of maintaining a healthy work-life balance and supports employees in managing their personal and family responsibilities.
The Company promotes family-friendly practices through:

The Company also encourages employees to maintain a balance between professional commitments and personal wellbeing.
## Health Insurance & Medical Benefits
The Company is committed to supporting employee health, wellbeing, and financial protection by providing Group Health Insurance coverage to eligible employees under the Company’s approved medical insurance scheme.
- Eligible employees shall be covered under the Company’s Group Health Insurance Policy as per Company eligibility criteria and insurer enrollment requirements
- The current medical insurance coverage is provided under the “Flexi Health Protect Plan (Group)” issued by Bajaj General Insurance Limited
- The Group Health Insurance Policy currently provides a Sum Insured coverage of up to INR 3,00,000 per eligible employee, subject to policy terms, conditions, exclusions, and insurer guidelines
- Insurance coverage shall remain valid only during the active employment period and policy validity period as approved by the Company
- Coverage may include hospitalization expenses, medical treatment, emergency care, and other benefits covered under the applicable insurance policy terms
- The Company may extend insurance benefits to eligible dependents, family members, spouse, or children based on employee category, policy structure, and management approval
- All insurance claims, hospitalization support, approvals, and reimbursements shall be processed in accordance with the insurer’s claim procedures and applicable policy conditions
- Employees shall promptly intimate HR and/or the insurance support team regarding hospitalization, medical emergencies, or claim-related requirements
- Employees are required to provide accurate personal, nominee, and dependent information along with all necessary supporting documents for enrollment and claim processing
- Any false declaration, fraudulent claim, concealment of facts, misuse of insurance benefits, or submission of forged medical documents may result in disciplinary action, recovery proceedings, cancellation of benefits, and legal action, wherever applicable
- The Company reserves the right to revise, renew, modify, suspend, or discontinue the insurance policy, insurer, coverage amount, premium contribution structure, dependent coverage, or related benefits based on business requirements, policy renewal terms, or insurer conditions

chapters.title: leave
chapters.text:
The employees of New Life Medicals Private Limited are entitled to Leave of 24 days per annum.
In addition to the standard leave entitlement, employees may avail the following types of leave as applicable:
- Sick Leave: Granted in case of illness or medical conditions, subject to approval
- Casual Leave: For personal or urgent requirements
- Earned Leave: As per company policy and accumulation rules
Female employees shall be entitled to maternity benefits in accordance with the provisions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 and other applicable Indian labour laws.
- Eligible female employees shall be entitled to up to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two surviving children, out of which not more than 8 weeks shall precede the expected date of delivery
- In case of the third child or subsequent children, the employee shall be entitled to 12 weeks of paid maternity leave
- Leave shall also cover childbirth, miscarriage, medical termination of pregnancy, tubectomy operation, and related medical care as applicable under law
- Employees are required to inform the Company in advance and submit relevant medical documents and certificates
- Maternity benefits, salary payment during leave, nursing breaks, and other protections shall be provided in accordance with statutory provisions
Male employees may be granted paternity leave to support their family during childbirth.
- Male employees may be granted up to 7 days of paid paternity leave for childbirth-related family support
- Paternity leave should normally be availed within 30 days from the date of childbirth
- Prior approval from the reporting manager and HR department shall be required
- Employees may be required to submit supporting documents such as birth records or hospital documents, if requested by the Company
## Bereavement Leave
Employees may avail leave in case of death of immediate family members.
All leaves must be applied and approved through the prescribed process.
[table]
| Leave Type | Eligibility | Description | Remarks |
| Casual Leave (CL) | Up to 7 days per year | For personal or urgent work | Prior approval required |
| Sick Leave (SL) | Up to 7 days per year | For illness or medical reasons | Medical certificate may be required |
| Earned Leave (EL) / Privilege Leave | 15 days per year | Planned leave for personal use | Can be carried forward as per policy |
| Maternity Leave | Up to 26 weeks (for first two children) | For childbirth and related care | As per Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 |
| Maternity Leave (3rd child onwards) | Up to 12 weeks | For childbirth (third child onwards) | As per law |
| Paternity Leave | Up to 5 days | For male employees during childbirth | To be availed within 15 days of birth |
| Bereavement Leave | Up to 3 days | In case of death of immediate family member | Immediate intimation required |
## LTA
LTA can be availed by an employee once in every financial year, i.e. between 1st April to 31st March, as per their eligibility.
## CONDITIONS FOR AVAILING LTA :
LTA can be availed only after confirmation.
- It is mandatory for the employee to avail at least 3 days of Earned Leaves for the purpose of claiming LTA and provide actual supporting bills for claiming exemptions.
- Hotel stay and other lodging expenses are not admissible for claim under LTA.
- There will not be any cash advance towards this purpose. Reimbursement shall be given only against bills and travel documents.
- As per Income Tax Rules, the LTA can be availed of twice in a block of four calendar years, without attracting tax, subject to employees providing a declaration and production of proof of journey.

chapters.title: Emergency Preparedness, Response and Evacuation Procedures
chapters.text:
The Company shall establish emergency preparedness and response procedures to minimize risks associated with fire, medical emergencies, natural disasters, chemical incidents, electrical failures, security threats, or other workplace emergencies.
Emergency preparedness measures may include:
- Identification and display of emergency exits and evacuation routes
- Installation and maintenance of firefighting and emergency response equipment
- Conducting emergency evacuation drills and mock exercises periodically
- Providing emergency response instructions and awareness to employees
- Availability of first-aid kits, emergency contacts, and medical assistance facilities
- Designation of trained emergency response personnel wherever applicable
- Immediate reporting and escalation of emergency situations
- Coordination with local emergency authorities whenever required
During emergency situations, employees are expected to:
- Remain calm and cooperate with emergency response personnel
- Follow evacuation procedures and safety instructions
- Avoid panic, obstruction, or unsafe behaviour
- Report injuries, hazards, or emergency concerns immediately
- Proceed to designated assembly points during evacuation
Failure to comply with emergency procedures may endanger workplace safety and may result in disciplinary action.
## Health and Safety Training, Awareness and Employee Participation
The Company believes that continuous training and employee participation are essential for maintaining an effective workplace health and safety culture.
The Company may conduct:
- General workplace safety orientation programs
- Periodic health and safety awareness sessions
- Emergency response and evacuation training
- Fire safety and first-aid awareness programs
- Safe equipment handling and operational safety training
- PPE usage and safety compliance training
- Behaviour-based safety awareness initiatives
- Contractor and visitor safety briefings wherever applicable
Employees are expected to:
- Attend mandatory health and safety training programs
- Follow safety instructions provided during training sessions
- Actively participate in workplace safety initiatives
- Apply learned safety practices during daily operations
- Support the Company in improving workplace health and safety performance
The Company encourages employees to contribute suggestions, observations, and recommendations for improving workplace safety standards and reducing operational risks.
## ncident Reporting, Investigation and Corrective Action
All workplace accidents, injuries, occupational illnesses, unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, property damage incidents, environmental incidents, and near misses must be reported immediately to the designated authority or reporting manager.
The Company shall:
- Maintain procedures for incident reporting and investigation
- Conduct fair, timely, and impartial investigations of workplace incidents
- Identify root causes, contributing factors, and system gaps
- Implement corrective and preventive measures to avoid recurrence
- Maintain records of incidents, investigations, and corrective actions
- Monitor implementation and effectiveness of corrective measures
Employees are expected to cooperate fully during investigations and provide complete and accurate information related to workplace incidents.
## Employee Responsibilities and Safety Compliance
Every employee has a personal responsibility to contribute towards maintaining a safe, secure, and healthy workplace environment.
Employees are expected to:
- Comply with all Company health and safety procedures, rules, and instructions
- Use personal protective equipment (PPE) wherever required
- Operate workplace equipment and machinery responsibly
- Maintain workplace discipline, cleanliness, and hygiene
- Report hazards, incidents, injuries, or unsafe conditions promptly
- Avoid horseplay, negligence, violence, or unsafe behaviour
- Support workplace safety initiatives and emergency preparedness measures
- Respect the safety and wellbeing of fellow employees and stakeholders
Violation of workplace health and safety requirements, negligence, intentional unsafe conduct, or failure to comply with safety instructions may result in disciplinary action in accordance with Company policies and applicable laws.

chapters.title: Recruitment & Selection Procedure
chapters.text:
The Company follows a structured recruitment and selection process to ensure fairness, transparency, equal opportunity, and selection of suitable talent aligned with organizational requirements.
## Workforce Planning & Manpower Requisition
- Department Heads identify manpower requirements based on operational needs, business expansion, replacement requirements, succession planning, or project requirements
- Approved manpower requisitions are submitted to HR and management for recruitment approval
- Recruitment is initiated only after necessary approvals from authorized management personnel
## Job Description & Position Requirements
- HR and the concerned department prepare or review the Job Description (JD), required qualifications, experience criteria, technical competencies, behavioral expectations, and reporting structure for the position
- Recruitment criteria are defined strictly based on job-related requirements and business needs
## Sourcing of Candidates
- Candidates are sourced through job portals, recruitment agencies, employee referrals, campus recruitment, social platforms, internal job postings, professional networks, consultants, and other lawful recruitment channels
- Internal employees are provided equal opportunity to apply for suitable vacancies through internal mobility or promotion opportunities wherever applicable
## Equal Opportunity Commitment
- The Company provides equal employment opportunity to all eligible candidates and employees without discrimination of any kind
- Recruitment, promotion, compensation, training, career development, and internal mobility decisions are based on merit, competency, qualifications, performance, and business requirements
- The Company encourages diversity, inclusion, and fair representation within the workforce
- Reasonable accommodation and support are provided to eligible persons with disabilities wherever reasonably practicable and operationally feasible
## Screening & Selection Process
- Applications are screened based on qualifications, experience, technical competency, behavioral suitability, and role requirements
- Shortlisted candidates undergo interviews, assessments, technical evaluations, practical tests, HR discussions, or other selection procedures depending on the role requirements
- Interview evaluations are conducted objectively and professionally by authorized interview panel members
- Selection decisions are based on merit, suitability for the role, organizational fit, and business requirements
## Background Verification & Documentation
- Selected candidates are required to submit necessary employment, educational, identity, address, and statutory documents as requested by the Company
- The Company conducts background verification, reference checks, qualification verification, and other due diligence procedures wherever applicable
- Submission of false information, forged documents, concealment of facts, or misrepresentation during recruitment may result in withdrawal of offer, disciplinary action, or termination of employment
## Offer of Employment & Onboarding
- Selected candidates receive a formal employment offer or appointment letter containing applicable terms and conditions of employment
- New employees undergo onboarding, induction, policy orientation, safety briefing, compliance training, and role familiarization programs as applicable
- Employees are required to comply with all Company policies, code of conduct, confidentiality requirements, and statutory obligations from the date of joining
## Recruitment Compliance & Confidentiality
- All recruitment activities are conducted in accordance with applicable labour laws, equal opportunity principles, ethical business practices, and Company policies
- Candidate information, interview records, assessment results, and personal data are handled confidentially and used only for lawful recruitment purposes
- The Company reserves the right to modify, suspend, cancel, or close any recruitment process or vacancy based on organizational requirements and management discretion
## Anti-Harassment, Anti-Discrimination & Respectful Workplace Policy
New Life Medical Private Limited is committed to maintaining a safe, respectful, inclusive, ethical, and professional work environment free from harassment, discrimination, bullying, retaliation, victimization, and inappropriate workplace behavior.
The Company maintains zero tolerance towards any form of harassment, discrimination, abusive conduct, intimidation, retaliation, or unfair treatment at the workplace or during any work-related interaction, activity, travel, communication, or event.
The Company strictly prohibits discrimination or harassment on the basis of gender, age, religion, caste, race, ethnicity, marital status, disability, pregnancy, nationality, social background, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable laws.

chapters.title: Prevention of Sexual Harassment
chapters.text:
The Company is committed to providing a safe and secure workplace free from sexual harassment, in accordance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.
Sexual harassment includes:
- Unwelcome physical contact or advances
- Demand or request for sexual favours
- Making sexually coloured remarks
- Showing inappropriate or explicit content
- Any unwelcome verbal, non-verbal, or physical conduct
The Company has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) as per legal requirements.
Employees are encouraged to report any such incidents.
- Complaint must be submitted within 3 months of the incident
- Inquiry shall be completed within 90 days
- Strict confidentiality shall be maintained
- No retaliation against complainant
Any violation will lead to disciplinary action, including termination.
The Company is committed to providing a safe, secure, and respectful workplace for all employees. Any form of sexual harassment at the workplace is strictly prohibited.
This policy is implemented in accordance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act) and applicable rules.
Sexual harassment includes, but is not limited to:
- Unwelcome physical contact or advances
- Demand or request for sexual favours
- Making sexually coloured remarks or inappropriate jokes
- Displaying or sharing offensive or explicit content
- Any unwelcome verbal, non-verbal, or physical conduct of a sexual nature
All employees are expected to maintain professional behaviour and respect the dignity of others at all times.
The Company has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) to address complaints related to sexual harassment.
## Complaint and Remediation procedure

chapters.title: Grievance Redressal Procedure
chapters.text:
New Life Medical Private Limited is committed to maintaining a fair, transparent, respectful, ethical, and positive workplace environment where employees are encouraged to openly communicate workplace concerns, complaints, disputes, or grievances without fear of retaliation, intimidation, discrimination, or unfair treatment.
The Company recognizes that timely identification and resolution of workplace concerns contribute significantly towards employee wellbeing, workplace harmony, operational efficiency, employee engagement, and organizational growth. Accordingly, the Company has established a structured grievance redressal mechanism to ensure that employee concerns are handled fairly, professionally, confidentially, and within a reasonable timeframe.
The grievance procedure provides employees with an opportunity to raise concerns relating to workplace behaviour, employment conditions, supervision, communication, safety, facilities, compensation, policies, discrimination, harassment, work allocation, interpersonal conflicts, or any other employment-related issue affecting the employee’s work environment or professional wellbeing.
## Objective of the Grievance Procedure
The objective of the grievance procedure is to:
- Promote a healthy, respectful, collaborative, and transparent workplace culture
- Provide employees with a formal mechanism to raise workplace concerns and complaints
- Ensure grievances are reviewed and resolved fairly, objectively, and confidentially
- Encourage open communication and professional conflict resolution practices
- Prevent escalation of workplace disputes and operational disruption
- Protect employees from retaliation, victimization, harassment, or unfair treatment arising from genuine complaints
- Improve employee satisfaction, trust, engagement, and workplace wellbeing
- Strengthen organizational accountability, ethical conduct, and professional workplace practices
## Scope of Grievances
Employees may raise grievances relating to, including but not limited to:
- Harassment, discrimination, bullying, retaliation, victimization, or inappropriate workplace conduct
- Employee health and Safety
- Human rights including labor exfoliation
- Interpersonal conflicts, communication gaps, or behavioural concerns between employees, supervisors, or departments
- Working conditions, workplace facilities, health & safety concerns, hygiene, or operational practices
- Compensation, benefits, incentives, leave management, attendance, or payroll-related concerns
- Performance evaluation, role clarity, workload allocation, reporting structure, or career development concerns
- Violation of Company policies, ethical standards, compliance obligations, or professional conduct requirements
- Unfair treatment, biased decision-making, or misuse of authority by any employee or supervisor
- Concerns relating to transfers, mobility, training opportunities, or employment practices
- Any other workplace-related issue impacting employee wellbeing, dignity, productivity, or professional environment
## Grievance Reporting Mechanism
- Employees are encouraged to initially discuss and attempt to resolve concerns with their immediate reporting manager wherever reasonably practicable and appropriate
- In situations where the employee is uncomfortable approaching the reporting manager, or where the matter remains unresolved, the grievance may be escalated directly to the HR Department or designated management authority
- Employees may raise grievances verbally, through written application, email communication, official reporting channels, meetings, or any other authorized grievance reporting mechanism established by the Company.
- Grievance officer: email: - XYZ@gmail.com
- Employees are encouraged to report grievances promptly and provide complete facts, supporting documents, evidence, witness details, or relevant information wherever applicable
- Anonymous complaints may be reviewed by the Company wherever sufficient information is available to conduct an appropriate assessment or investigation
## Grievance Review & Investigation Process
- Upon receipt of a grievance, HR and/or the designated authority shall acknowledge the complaint within 3 working days
- Preliminary assessment and review of the grievance shall normally be initiated within 7 working days from the date of receipt of the complaint
- Depending upon the nature and seriousness of the grievance, the Company may conduct meetings, interviews, discussions, fact-finding reviews, document verification, or internal investigations
- All employees are expected to cooperate honestly, professionally, and confidentially during grievance investigations and related proceedings
- Investigations shall be conducted fairly, impartially, objectively, and without bias, discrimination, retaliation, or conflict of interest
